value.name: Whitfield ends his reading
value.description: Whitfield looks up from the page he had been turning and sets it down without marking his place, signaling that Asha's long wait is over.
evidence: Whitfield looked up from the page he had been turning and set it down without marking his place
the seventeen minutes she had spent at the door were now spent

value.name: Asha enters and sits across from Whitfield
value.description: Asha crosses to the chair opposite Whitfield, places her briefcase on her knees, and delays opening it.
evidence: She crossed to the chair across from him and laid the briefcase flat on her knees and did not open it yet

value.name: Asha ignores Devin's unanswered text
value.description: Asha notices that Devin's text remains unanswered on her phone and realizes she has already shifted the consequences of her choice away from herself.
evidence: Devin's text was still on the phone in her coat pocket, unanswered
the choice she had made by not stepping into the stairwell had not closed the question of Devin so much as moved it

value.name: Asha realizes her words will reach Devin secondhand
value.description: Asha understands that whatever she tells Whitfield will be relayed to Devin as something already said, and that Devin's own call will reach the firm without her control.
evidence: whatever she told Whitfield in the next half hour would now reach Devin as a thing already said
whatever Devin had been calling to tell her at five forty-three would reach the firm through a door she no longer controlled

value.name: Whitfield asks what Asha came to say
value.description: Whitfield asks Asha directly what she has come in to tell him, indicating that he already knows the meeting is unusual.
evidence: Whitfield asked her, in the level voice he used when he already knew the meeting was not routine, what she had come in to tell him

value.name: Asha anticipates explaining herself to Devin
value.description: Asha realizes the harder problem is not what she tells Whitfield now but how she will later explain it to Devin, who will hear it secondhand and judge her memory against his own.
evidence: Asha, hearing the question land in the room, knew that the harder problem was not what she said to him now but what she would have to say to Devin after
when the protege she had refused to call first heard the account secondhand and had to decide what his own memory was worth against hers

value.name: Asha leaves Whitfield's office
value.description: Asha exits Whitfield's office carrying a briefcase that feels lighter to her, despite nothing having been removed from it.
evidence: Asha left Whitfield's office with the briefcase lighter in her hand than it had been on the way in
which made no sense because nothing had come out of it that had not gone back

value.name: Asha checks her phone in the elevator
value.description: In the elevator down to the garage, Asha finally turns her phone face up to see what Devin had sent or called.
evidence: In the elevator down to the garage she finally turned the phone face up
